name: Drevsin Ube-Black Pepper Mood Gels
description: Soft, jewel-toned gel candies in ube-black pepper flavor, each containing a micro-dose of licensed anxiolytic bioactives designed to produce mild calm without sedation. Sold in blister packs of eight, each gel a deep violet color with visible spice flecks.
flavor_profile: Sweet ube earthiness with a slow-building black pepper warmth; the heat arrives after the gel dissolves, creating a pleasant contrast with the calming effect
cultural_context: Drevsin gels occupy the respectable end of mood-candy — licensed, dosage-controlled, sold in pharmacies and upscale vending. Tier 3 professionals use them before high-stakes presentations or difficult commutes. Tier 4 users consider them slightly beneath them but keep a pack in the drawer. There is social stigma in some communities about visible mood-candy use; others wear it as a badge of self-awareness.
story_hooks: Someone has been systematically buying out specific pharmacy locations' Drevsin stock in a pattern that, when mapped, traces a corridor through the city — not a supply shortage, a signal.
A Tier 4 executive has been using Drevsin gels in quantities that suggest the anxiolytic dose is being used to suppress something more than work stress.
The licensed bioactive in Drevsin gels has a rare interaction with a common BCI firmware version — it doesn't harm users, but it produces a brief 3-second gap in memory recording.
